content.section_summary: Urgent electrical cardioversion is recommended for acute worsening heart failure (HF) with rapid ventricular rates and hemodynamic instability, after assessing thromboembolic risk. If AF onset >48 hours and patient not on chronic oral anticoagulation, at least 3 weeks of therapeutic anticoagulation or transoesophageal echocardiography is required before cardioversion. When pharmacological cardioversion is preferred, amiodarone is the drug of choice; other antiarrhythmics (propafenone, flecainide, dronedarone) are associated with worse outcomes in HFrEF. Catheter ablation can improve prognosis in selected HFrEF patients but trial results vary by population and design.

recommendations.urgent_cardioversion: Indicated in acute worsening HF with rapid ventricular rates and hemodynamic instability, after thromboembolic risk assessment.
recommendations.pre_cardioversion_anticoagulation: If AF onset >48 h and not on chronic oral anticoagulant, require ≥3 weeks of therapeutic anticoagulation or transoesophageal echocardiography prior to cardioversion.
recommendations.pharmacological_cardioversion: Amiodarone preferred in patients with HF; other antiarrhythmics (propafenone, flecainide, dronedarone) linked to worse outcomes in HFrEF.

pharmacological_notes.amiodarone: Favoured when pharmacological cardioversion is chosen; can help maintain sinus rhythm after cardioversion in HF patients.
pharmacological_notes.other_antiarrhythmics: Propafenone, flecainide, dronedarone and similar agents are associated with worse outcomes in HFrEF and thus are less suitable.

trial_summaries.name: EAST-AFNET 4
trial_summaries.population: Early AF patients (28.6% with HF enrolled)
trial_summaries.outcome: Stopped early for lower occurrence of primary outcome (death, stroke, or hospitalization for worsening HF or ACS) in early rhythm control vs usual care.
trial_summaries.notes: Patients assigned to rhythm control had closer follow-up; catheter ablation performed in minority (19.4%) of rhythm control arm.

trial_summaries.name: CASTLE-AF
trial_summaries.population: 363 patients with persistent or paroxysmal AF, LVEF <35%, implanted device (ICD or CRT-D)

results.hazard_ratio_info: HR reported with 95% CI (example shown 0.62; 0.43–0.87 in text)

trial_summaries.conclusion: Catheter ablation reduced primary endpoint and some other endpoints (all-cause/CV death or worsening HF) in this highly selected population, but trial had selection and crossover limitations.

trial_summaries.name: CABANA
trial_summaries.population: Investigator-initiated, open-label, multicentre randomized trial enrolling 2204 symptomatic AF patients
trial_summaries.primary_outcome: Composite of death, disabling stroke, serious bleeding, or cardiac arrest
trial_summaries.result: Failed to show benefit of AF ablation over medical care for primary composite endpoint in overall population.
trial_summaries.notes: Number of events small; LVEF available in 73% and definitions varied across cases.

trial_summaries.name: AMICA
trial_summaries.population: Patients with HFrEF and persistent AF randomized to catheter ablation or medical therapy (n approximately 140 reported)
trial_summaries.result: Failed to show a difference in LVEF increase between groups in first trial mentioned.
trial_summaries.notes: Small trial; contrasted with other trials showing benefit.

trial_summaries.name: AATAC
trial_summaries.population: Patients with HFrEF and persistent AF randomized to catheter ablation or amiodarone (n approximately 203 reported)
trial_summaries.results: Second trial showed superiority of catheter ablation with respect to AF recurrence, reduction in unplanned hospitalizations and mortality, and benefit on LVEF.
trial_summaries.notes: AATAC showed benefit on LVEF and clinical outcomes in contrast to AMICA; consistent with CASTLE-AF findings.

content.overall_interpretation: Catheter ablation may improve prognosis and symptoms in selected patients with HFrEF and AF, but results depend on trial selection, endpoints, and patient characteristics. Amiodarone remains preferred for pharmacological cardioversion in HF. Decisions should consider thromboembolic risk, LVEF, device status, and trial-specific applicability.
